tips.title: When someone dies at home, establish whether the death is natural or unnatural before you move anything
tips.cost: The police case and a post-mortem at a government hospital are free. A private ambulance, a private mortuary and the funeral cost money.
tips.inPlainWords: If the death was expected and a doctor was treating the person, call the doctor and the family; the doctor can certify the cause. If the death is sudden, unexplained, accidental, suicidal or violent, call 112 and do not move the body or disturb the room. The police register the case, hold the scene and arrange a post-mortem. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 the police inquire into an unnatural or suspicious death and report it to the Executive Magistrate, who may hold an inquiry into the cause of death. Cremation or burial needs the death registered first.
tips.benefit: Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 requires the police to inquire into a death by suicide or a suspicious death and to report it to the Executive Magistrate, and the body is sent for medical examination. Section 196 lets a Magistrate hold an inquiry into the cause of death. The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 requires the death to be registered before cremation or burial. A medical certificate of cause of death comes from the doctor who treated the person, or from the hospital.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs, Emergency Response Support System. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not cremate, bury or embalm before the death is registered and, in an unnatural case, before the police give clearance. Keep the case number, the doctor's certificate and the post-mortem report. A hospital death is certified by the hospital; a home death by the treating doctor or the medical officer of the area.

tips.title: The death certificate is the key document: the doctor certifies the cause and the municipal registrar registers it
tips.cost: The registration fee is small; a late fee applies after 21 days.
tips.inPlainWords: A death must be registered with the local municipal registrar under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. A hospital issues a medical certificate of cause of death; for a death at home, the doctor who treated the person or the medical officer certifies it. The registrar issues the death certificate, usually within 21 days. You need it for the cremation, the insurance claim, the pension and the succession.
tips.benefit: The 1969 Act requires registration within 21 days; a late registration needs the registrar's permission and a fee. The certificate is issued in Form 4 or Form 5. A hospital death is reported by the hospital; a home death is reported by the family. The certificate is the basis for the EPF, ESIC, insurance and bank claims. A corrected certificate can be issued if there is an error.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs, civil registration. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A death certificate is not a succession certificate. Keep several copies. If the cause of death is unnatural, the police and the post-mortem report come first.

tips.title: Who may move, store and cremate the body is set by the municipality and the police, not by the hospital
tips.cost: Cremation at a municipal crematorium has a small fee, and many municipal bodies charge nothing for a resident. A private crematorium, an ambulance and a priest cost more. Cold storage in a government mortuary is free.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national rule that only a funeral home may move, embalm or cremate a body, and no three-day limit in the statute book. A crematorium or burial ground run by a municipal body or a panchayat must be licensed by that body, and the health officer controls the removal of a body from a hospital. A hospital mortuary keeps a body in cold storage, but in an unnatural death it stays there until the police and the post-mortem release it. Ask the hospital's medical officer and the municipal office who may take the body and which papers are needed. A body going to another state or abroad needs written clearance and embalming.
tips.benefit: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 requires the death to be registered before cremation or burial, and the person in charge of a crematorium or burial ground must see that the death is registered. Municipal corporation and municipal council Acts license crematoria and burial grounds and let the health officer regulate the removal and burial of bodies. State rules and the police control the release of a body in a medico-legal case. Any storage limit comes from the hospital's mortuary rules or the municipal by-laws, not from a national statute.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://www.mohfw.gov.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs. <https://www.mha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not let an agent move the body before the hospital and the police release it. Ask for the entry in the mortuary register. An unregistered crematorium is a health risk and a legal problem; check the licence at the gate.

tips.title: If the cause of death is disputed, ask the police and the Magistrate for a post-mortem before the body is released
tips.cost: A police-ordered post-mortem at a government hospital is free. A private examination, a lawyer and court fees cost money.
tips.inPlainWords: In India a post-mortem is ordered by the police in an unnatural or suspicious death; the family has no statutory right to demand one by itself. If you doubt the cause, tell the investigating officer in writing and ask the Sub-divisional Magistrate to order an inquiry into the cause of death. Do it while the body is still in the mortuary, because once it is cremated the evidence is gone. Ask the hospital for a copy of the medical records and the inquest papers, and keep the post-mortem report.
tips.benefit: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 the police must inquire into a suspicious or unnatural death and send the body to a medical officer for examination, and a Magistrate may hold an inquiry into the cause of death. A post-mortem is done at a government hospital, usually by a board of doctors, when the police or the Magistrate requires it. If the report is disputed, the family can ask the Magistrate for a further inquiry and, in an exceptional case, for exhumation. Medical records belong to the patient, and the family can get copies from the hospital.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://www.mohfw.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The 48-hour and seven-day windows in the source edition are not Indian rules; the practical deadline is the release of the body. Do not accept a certificate that states no cause of death without asking why. Keep the inquest papers, the post-mortem report and the hospital file together.

tips.title: After a death, register it and settle the accounts — India has no household-register cancellation step
tips.cost: The death certificate is cheap. A succession certificate involves court fees and a lawyer.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not have a household-register cancellation. The steps are: register the death, obtain the death certificate, inform the bank, the insurer, the EPFO and the pension office, and settle the estate. Surrender or transfer the ration card, the gas connection and the vehicle registration where needed. Keep the death certificate and the legal-heir documents for every claim.
tips.benefit: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 and the municipal rules govern the death certificate. The EPF Scheme, 1952 and the ESIC scheme provide for a nominee or a legal heir. The Insurance Act, 1938 and the policy terms govern a life-insurance claim. A bank account with a nomination can be released to the nominee; without one, a succession certificate or a will may be needed.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A nomination is not a will, and it can be challenged by another heir. Do not withdraw the balance before the bank's process is complete. Keep the funeral receipt and the death certificate.

tips.title: There is no statutory list of basic funeral services in India: ask for an itemised quote and buy only what you need
tips.cost: A municipal cremation is cheap or free for a resident; a private package is priced by the market. The itemised quote costs nothing.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national list of basic funeral services with prices fixed by law. A municipal crematorium or burial ground publishes its own charges and often charges a resident little or nothing; a private funeral home sets its own package. Before you agree, ask for an itemised quote: transport, cold storage, embalming, the shroud, the priest, the wood or gas, the urn, the slot. Decide which of these you actually want and refuse the rest. Compare the municipal rate with the private package before you sign.
tips.benefit: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 makes a misleading price or a hidden charge an unfair trade practice, and a service short of what was promised a deficiency. A crematorium run by a municipal body publishes its charges, and many municipal bodies provide cremation free or at a nominal fee for a resident. The Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and the packaged-commodity rules require a displayed price for goods sold by weight or in a package. None of these fixes a national funeral tariff, so the quote and the receipt are your protection.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; e-Daakhil consumer portal. <https://edaakhil.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A basic and non-basic split is the seller's marketing, not a legal category. Ask the municipal rate before you accept a private package. Keep the quote, the bill and a photograph of the price board.

tips.title: If you are bundled, overcharged or split-billed, note it and complain: consumer law is the route in India
tips.cost: The helpline is free. Filing on e-Daakhil carries a small fee that depends on the claim, and a lawyer is optional.
tips.inPlainWords: Forced bundling, a charge above the quoted price and one service split into several line items are unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. On the spot, ask for the itemised bill and the price list, pay under protest if you must, and keep the bill, the receipt and a photograph of the price board. Then call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 or file on the e-Daakhil portal. A complaint can be filed in the District Consumer Commission where you live, and a municipal crematorium's overcharge can also go to the municipal commissioner.
tips.benefit: The 2019 Act covers goods and services, including a funeral service, and gives a consumer the right to be informed of the price, to choose and to seek redressal. A misleading price or a hidden charge is an unfair trade practice; a service delivered short of what was promised is a deficiency. A complaint can be filed online through e-Daakhil, and the helpline 1915 can take a grievance to the company first. For a municipal crematorium, the local body's grievance cell and the municipal commissioner are the faster route.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs, National Consumer Helpline. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; e-Daakhil. <https://edaakhil.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A complaint needs the bill and a written account of what was demanded. Do not sign a no-further-claim line at the counter. Keep a copy of the death certificate with the papers.

tips.title: Funeral agents are not registered with any Indian authority: check the trade licence, the GSTIN and the hospital's vendor list
tips.cost: Checking a GSTIN and a trade licence is free. An agent's commission is not.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not register funeral agents or funeral-goods shops with a civil-affairs office, and there is no official list to look them up on. A legitimate business has a municipal trade licence, a shop-and-establishment registration, a GSTIN and, if it handles bodies, a working arrangement with a hospital or crematorium. Ask for the GSTIN and check it on the GST portal, ask the hospital's medical officer which vendors it allows inside, and do not pay a deposit to an agent who cannot show an address and a bill.
tips.benefit: A shop or agency needs a municipal trade licence and, above the turnover threshold, a GST registration; a company or a firm is on the register kept by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. A hospital's empanelment list and the crematorium's own counter are the practical check, because an unauthorised agent who collects money at a hospital gate has no registration to lose. There is no Indian register of funeral intermediaries, so verify the business itself rather than a licence that does not exist.
tips.sources: Goods and Services Tax portal. <https://www.gst.gov.in/>; Ministry of Corporate Affairs. <https://www.mca.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://www.mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not hand cash to someone who approaches you in a hospital corridor. Ask for a bill with the GSTIN printed on it. If an agent demands money to release the body, speak to the hospital's medical officer or the police.

tips.title: Collect the scattered funds: EPF, ESIC, pension, insurance, bank balances and any work-related benefit
tips.cost: The forms are free. A succession certificate involves court fees.
tips.inPlainWords: After a death, the money is spread across accounts: the EPF and EPS pension, ESIC dependants' benefit, a life-insurance policy, bank balances and a pension. Each has its own form and nominee rule. Start with the death certificate and the legal-heir documents, and ask each institution for its claim form. Do not pay an agent a percentage to 'trace' the money.
tips.benefit: The EPFO pays the provident-fund balance and the EPS pension to the nominee or the family. ESIC pays dependants' benefit where the death is an employment injury. A life insurer pays the nominee under the policy. A bank releases a nominated deposit to the nominee, and an un-nominated deposit needs a succession certificate or a will. The Insurance Act and the EPF Scheme set the procedure.
tips.sources: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, nominations. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A nominee holds the money for the legal heirs; it is not a substitute for a will. The employer may also owe a gratuity or leave encashment. Keep the acknowledgement for every claim.

tips.title: After a death, relatives have no automatic right to the person's data in India: a nominee named in advance, or a court, is the route
tips.cost: Asking the platform is free. A court application needs a lawyer unless you qualify for free legal aid.
tips.inPlainWords: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 protects the data of a living person. It does not give a relative the right to demand access to, copies of, correction of or deletion of a dead person's data. The Act does let a person nominate someone in advance, and that nominee can exercise the rights after death or incapacity; if nobody was named, ask the platform in writing, and if it refuses, take legal advice about a court application. Money is different: a bank deposit, an insurance policy and a pension are claimed by a nominee or a legal heir under their own rules.
tips.benefit: Section 14 of the 2023 Act creates a right to nominate an individual who may exercise the data principal's rights on death or incapacity, in the manner prescribed by the rules. Outside that, an online account is governed by the platform's terms and by the general law, and a platform may require a court order before it hands over or deletes an account. A bank or an insurer settles a claim to a nominee or a legal heir under its own rules, and for a small deposit it follows a simplified procedure instead of a succession certificate.
tips.sources: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (text). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Deleting an account can destroy messages and records that an heir needs. Do not pay an agent who promises to unlock an account. Ask in writing and keep the reply. Free legal aid is available from the District Legal Services Authority and the National Legal Services Authority helpline.

tips.title: Heirs pay the deceased's debts only out of the estate they inherit, not from their own money
tips.cost: A probate or a succession certificate costs money; a lawyer is advisable for a large estate.
tips.inPlainWords: Under Indian succession law, an heir is liable for the deceased's debts only to the extent of the estate received. If the debts exceed the assets, the heir can refuse the inheritance or let the estate be administered by the court. A secured creditor can enforce the mortgage against the property. A formal renunciation or a probate may be needed.
tips.benefit: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 and the personal laws govern inheritance; the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 governs the execution of a decree against the estate. A creditor can sue the legal representative, but recovery is limited to the estate's value. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 provides a route where the estate is insolvent. A will can name an executor.
tips.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India. <https://ibbi.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not sign a personal guarantee for the deceased's debt. A joint loan may make the surviving borrower liable. A secured asset can be repossessed even if the heir refuses the inheritance.

tips.title: Not every inheritance needs probate; a nominated bank deposit can be released on the bank's form
tips.cost: A nomination claim is free. A succession certificate or probate involves court fees and a lawyer.
tips.inPlainWords: Probate is not mandatory for every estate. A bank deposit with a valid nomination can be released to the nominee on the bank's claim form with the death certificate. Without a nomination, the bank may ask for a succession certificate, a probate or an indemnity, depending on the amount. A will still needs probate if it deals with immovable property in some jurisdictions.
tips.benefit: The RBI's customer-service rules and the bank's nomination scheme allow a nominee to receive a deposit. The Indian Succession Act, 1925 requires probate for a will in some cases, and the state rules vary. A succession certificate is issued by a civil court for debts and securities. A small estate may be settled with an affidavit and an indemnity, subject to the bank's policy.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, customer service. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A nominee is a trustee for the legal heirs, not necessarily the owner. A joint account with a survivorship clause passes to the survivor. Do not withdraw before the bank completes its process.
